From 19fc99d0c6ba7d9b65456496b5bb2169d5f74cd0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Nicolas Schichan <nschichan@freebox.fr>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2015 18:31:56 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] ARM: net fix emit_udiv() for BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_K
 intruction.

In that case, emit_udiv() will be called with rn == ARM_R0 (r_scratch)
and loading rm first into ARM_R0 will result in jit_udiv() function
being called the same dividend and divisor. Fix that by loading rn
first into ARM_R1 and then rm into ARM_R0.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas Schichan <nschichan@freebox.fr>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # v3.13+
Fixes: aee636c4809f (bpf: do not use reciprocal divide)
Acked-by: Mircea Gherzan <mgherzan@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/arch/arm/net/bpf_jit_32.c b/arch/arm/net/bpf_jit_32.c
index e1268f905026..f412b53ed268 100644
--- a/arch/arm/net/bpf_jit_32.c
+++ b/arch/arm/net/bpf_jit_32.c
@@ -449,10 +449,21 @@ static inline void emit_udiv(u8 rd, u8 rm, u8 rn, struct jit_ctx *ctx)
 		return;
 	}
 #endif
-	if (rm != ARM_R0)
-		emit(ARM_MOV_R(ARM_R0, rm), ctx);
+
+	/*
+	 * For BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_K instructions, rm is ARM_R4
+	 * (r_A) and rn is ARM_R0 (r_scratch) so load rn first into
+	 * ARM_R1 to avoid accidentally overwriting ARM_R0 with rm
+	 * before using it as a source for ARM_R1.
+	 *
+	 * For BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_X rm is ARM_R4 (r_A) and rn is
+	 * ARM_R5 (r_X) so there is no particular register overlap
+	 * issues.
+	 */
 	if (rn != ARM_R1)
 		emit(ARM_MOV_R(ARM_R1, rn), ctx);
+	if (rm != ARM_R0)
+		emit(ARM_MOV_R(ARM_R0, rm), ctx);
 
 	ctx->seen |= SEEN_CALL;
 	emit_mov_i(ARM_R3, (u32)jit_udiv, ctx);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `arch/arm/net/bpf_jit_32.c`**
- The function `emit_udiv()` has been modified to change the order of loading registers for the division operation.
- A comment block has been added to explain the reasoning behind the changes, specifically addressing the handling of registers for the `BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_K` instructions.
- The code now first loads the `rn` register into `ARM_R1` before loading the `rm` register into `ARM_R0`. This prevents the accidental overwriting of `ARM_R0` when `rn` is also `ARM_R0`.

### Relationships Between Modifications
- The changes in the `emit_udiv()` function are directly related to a bug fix for the handling of division operations in the BPF (Berkeley Packet Filter) context. The modification ensures that the correct values are used in the division operation by managing register usage more effectively.
- The added comments provide context for the changes, indicating that the fix is specifically for scenarios where `rn` and `rm` could overlap, which could lead to incorrect behavior in the division operation. This relationship highlights the importance of register management in low-level programming, particularly in the context of JIT (Just-In-Time) compilation for BPF.

Here is the commit message:
ARM: net fix emit_udiv() for BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_K
 intruction.

In that case, emit_udiv() will be called with rn == ARM_R0 (r_scratch)
and loading rm first into ARM_R0 will result in jit_udiv() function
being called the same dividend and divisor. Fix that by loading rn
first into ARM_R1 and then rm into ARM_R0.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas Schichan <nschichan@freebox.fr>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # v3.13+
Fixes: aee636c4809f (bpf: do not use reciprocal divide)
Acked-by: Mircea Gherzan <mgherzan@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurred because the `emit_udiv()` function was loading the `rm` register into `ARM_R0` first when both `rn` and `rm` could reference overlapping registers, specifically when `rn` was `ARM_R0` (r_scratch). This led to the `jit_udiv()` function being called with the same values for the dividend and divisor, resulting in incorrect behavior during division operations for `BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_K` instructions.

Here is the patch:
 
 static inline void emit_udiv(u8 rd, u8 rm, u8 rn, struct jit_ctx *ctx)
 {
 #if __LINUX_ARM_ARCH__ == 7
 	if (elf_hwcap & HWCAP_IDIVA) {
 		emit(ARM_UDIV(rd, rm, rn), ctx);
 		return;
 	}
 #endif
-	if (rm != ARM_R0)
-		emit(ARM_MOV_R(ARM_R0, rm), ctx);
+
+	/*
+	 * For BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_K instructions, rm is ARM_R4
+	 * (r_A) and rn is ARM_R0 (r_scratch) so load rn first into
+	 * ARM_R1 to avoid accidentally overwriting ARM_R0 with rm
+	 * before using it as a source for ARM_R1.
+	 *
+	 * For BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_X rm is ARM_R4 (r_A) and rn is
+	 * ARM_R5 (r_X) so there is no particular register overlap
+	 * issues.
+	 */
 	if (rn != ARM_R1)
 		emit(ARM_MOV_R(ARM_R1, rn), ctx);
+	if (rm != ARM_R0)
+		emit(ARM_MOV_R(ARM_R0, rm), ctx);
 
 	ctx->seen |= SEEN_CALL;
 	emit_mov_i(ARM_R3, (u32)jit_udiv, ctx);
 	emit_blx_r(ARM_R3, ctx);
 
 	if (rd != ARM_R0)
 		emit(ARM_MOV_R(rd, ARM_R0), ctx);
 }
